Reverified by exact-household requested-month replay on PolicyEngine 4.18.9, PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3, and PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3 (trace receipt SHA-256 8d2b138f4b068daf7d374972fe043ef58bc443a30c599b828d82e85a7fef7ccf). All four households consist only of members aged 17 or younger who carry positive weekly wages (persisted axiom input member_weekly_wages 4173.61 per member); PolicyEngine excludes all earnings of an imputed K-12 member age 17 or younger without requiring the co-resident-parent or parental-control condition in 7 CFR 273.9(c)(7), so its January snap_earned_income is 0.00 for every household and it pays a positive benefit. The minors-only household is valid under 273.1(a)(1), but wages count under 273.9(b)(1)(i), so axiom correctly fails the income gate (e.g. ecps-31462 gross 18793.09 against the 130 percent limit 1696.00 and the 200-percent-FPL BBCE screen 2660.00) and returns zero benefit. Exact-household requested-month replay on PolicyEngine 4.18.9, PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3, and PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3 (trace receipt SHA-256 8d2b138f4b068daf7d374972fe043ef58bc443a30c599b828d82e85a7fef7ccf). The bridge nets PolicyEngine's self-employment loss (after the 40 percent SNAP expense deduction but without PolicyEngine's zero floor) against wages when composing axiom's snap_gross_monthly_earned_income input, while PolicyEngine's own SNAP earned income floors self-employment at zero (snap_self_employment_income_after_expense_deduction = max(self_employment_income - expense_deduction, 0)); the two engines therefore receive different income inputs, and the row is a harness artifact, not a rule defect. For this household the persisted axiom earned-income input is -1579.25 per month while the replayed PolicyEngine monthly employment income is 7490.93 and monthly raw self-employment income is -15116.96: 7490.93 + 0.6 x -15116.96 = -1579.25, reproducing the netted input within 0.00. PolicyEngine counts the non-negative wage/unearned side (January snap_gross_income 7490.93) and is ineligible with zero benefit; axiom, fed the netted negative income, passes its income tests and pays 546.00. A dedicated tracking issue for the self-employment-loss netting in the Populace bridge still needs filing; axiom-oracles#397 documents the same unequal-cross-program-input policy problem for endogenous benefits.

The Populace bridge composes axiom's snap_gross_monthly_earned_income as wages plus 60 percent of PolicyEngine's raw self-employment income (a flat 40 percent SNAP expense deduction), while PolicyEngine's Florida parameters set the percentage self-employment expense deduction to zero (gov/usda/snap/income/deductions/self_employment/rate FL = 0, expense-based deduction applies), so PolicyEngine counts the full self-employment income when positive and floors losses at zero. The engines therefore received different earned-income inputs; both compute correctly from their own inputs, so the rows are harness artifacts. Every selected row is verified per-row: the direct January replay of the bridge input surface reproduces the committed PolicyEngine benefit to the cent, and the netting identity |wages + 0.6 x self_employment - axiom_input| <= 0.005 holds for all 43 rows. Representative row ecps-32387: axiom input 2004.07 = wages 0.00 + 0.6 x 3340.12; the benefit delta 320.30 matches 0.3 x 0.8 x 0.4 x self-employment (320.65) within rounding. A dedicated tracking issue for the bridge's flat 40 percent self-employment expense deduction still needs filing; axiom-oracles#397 documents the same unequal-input policy problem.
